correctness.rationale: For n>=3 and 0<δ<1, strict convexity of H=(1−δ)I+δ11^T yields a unique interior equilibrium q1 and a pathwise nonincreasing quadratic error potential. The prescribed strict ellipsoid implies ||e||_2<r and every coordinate update remains strictly interior, excluding clipping at all times. The identity e_i′=−δ(S−e_i) leads to S′=(1−δ)(S−e_i), Q′=Q−e_i²+δ²(S−e_i)² and exact averaging Σ(S−e_i)²=(n−2)S²+Q. This proves the displayed 2×2 evolution of E[S²],E[Q] for all steps. Strictly positive matrix entries and det(I−T)>0 imply 0<σ<ρ<1; from F_1≥(d/n)F_0 and σ<d/n, the Perron coefficient is strictly positive for every deterministic nonzero perturbation. Eigenvalue expansion gives both δ↑1 and n→∞ constants. Independent exact rational update-string enumeration matched each moment in four cases n=3..6 through depth four (81,256,625,1296 strings).
residual_risks: Sharp factor is in expectation of squared Euclidean error, not almost-sure pathwise exponent.

originality.rationale: The same Misiak–Dziubiński 2026 complete-network random-order public-good model has convergence bounds and numerical clique slowdown; it does not state the exact Euclidean two-moment matrix or universal initial-profile mean-square Perron factor. Gower–Richtárik randomized iterative method theory gives general expected squared norm inequalities rather than this special second-moment identity and its two sharp limits. A closely related Resultary entry on delayed two-coordinate Gauss–Seidel studies a different stochastic recurrence, not this game. The contribution is an exact symmetry reduction of an established algorithm, not a new general stochastic convergence theory.
